monthly_review.summary: You've significantly increased intensity this month, trading volume for higher-zone effort — reflected in faster pace, higher HR, and elevated aerobic TE, though total distance dropped.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 4 time jumped from 12% to 24% while Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 30%, indicating a pronounced shift toward threshold-intensity work — unusual for a recreational runner without concurrent recovery or volume support.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 remaining sessions (avg 4.2 km/session) to match last month’s 32.9 km — achievable with one long run (6–7 km), one moderate run (4.5 km), and one shorter tempo-adjacent run (4.2 km).

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm — meaning you’re moving farther per heartbeat at higher intensities, likely due to the recent 5.0 km run at 7:25/min/km (445 sec/km) with HR 163 and stride length 90.77 cm — your longest stride yet.

insights.title: Zone 2 volume collapsed while Zone 4 doubled
insights.body: Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 30% of total HR time, while Zone 4 surged from 12% to 24% — suggesting insufficient low-intensity recovery runs to support the jump in threshold work, increasing fatigue risk.

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with pace/HR shifts
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (slowest run, 9:00/min/km, HR 142) to 90.77 cm (fastest run, 7:25/min/km, HR 163), confirming neuromuscular adaptation under load — but ground contact time stayed stable (301–311 ms), indicating form resilience.

insights.title: Aerobic TE spiked without VO2 max change
insights.body: VO2 max remains flat at 34.0 mL/kg/min across all recent runs, yet aerobic TE rose to 4.6 on 2026-04-12 — signaling high acute stress without chronic adaptation yet, likely due to compressed session spacing (runs on 4/1, 4/3, 4/8, 4/12).

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) at 8:30–9:00 min/km on your next easy day, prioritizing cadence ≥152 spm and ground contact <305 ms.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Zone 2 volume (currently only 30%) and offset the 24% Zone 4 exposure — critical for mitochondrial development and recovery capacity.

recommendations.action: Insert a 20-min progressive run: start at 8:45 min/km (HR ~138), increase pace every 4 min to finish at 7:30 min/km (HR ~158), keeping vertical oscillation ≤8.2 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your 4/12 run hit 8.4 cm vertical oscillation at peak effort — this drill improves running economy while staying within safe HR progression (Z3→Z4 transition).

recommendations.action: Perform stride-length awareness drills before your next run: 4 × 100 m focusing on landing midfoot and extending stride by 2–3 cm vs your 70.96 cm baseline (from 4/1), then run 3.0 km at 8:15 min/km.
recommendations.reason: Your shortest stride (70.96 cm) occurred during your longest run (6.2 km) — suggesting fatigue-related form drop; targeted reinforcement builds consistency.

weekly_focus.description: Rebalance HR zone exposure by restoring Zone 2 foundation while preserving recent gains in Z4 efficiency — avoid adding new Z5 or extended Z4 until Zone 2 volume recovers to ≥40%.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5.0 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Form-focused short run with stride-length targets (3.0 km + drills)
